transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-14 09:00 PT
Duration: ~68 minutes (recorded)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (IT Ops), Ethan Reyes (FinOps), Lina Carter (Security), Noah Kim (Platform), Ava Thompson (Procurement), Samir Banerjee (Vendor Mgmt), Olivia Reed (Cloud Cost)

Summary:
Quick operational sync to align service-account delegation changes with vendor billing tags; surface any security gaps for upcoming vendor contract change; finalize owners for billing remap and KMS rotation steps.

Topics:
- Service-account delegation plan for internal automation and vendor access
- Vendor invoice -> service tag reconciliation (May run rate)
- KMS key rotation and service-account onboarding impacts
- Short-term monitoring/alerts for billing spikes
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: ok uh thanks everyone for joining, i think we can start — we got a fairly full agenda but quick, quick check: new vendor contract goes live next monday so we need to make sure service accounts and billing tags line up.
[00:18] Ethan Reyes: yeah and the finance side, we want to avoid a mass of untagged charges. last month there was some spillover from the pci test, so trying to prevent that again.
[00:29] Lina Carter: hi, im on — from security i want to call out that any delegation to vendor service accounts needs least privilege and documented key rotation steps. we noticed one of the service accounts still had long lived creds in last audit.
[00:42] Samir Banerjee: (Vendor Mgmt) hey, from vendor side we'll only use the service account you designate. but we do need read access to billing export, or at least a filtered view. is that something you can give us?
[00:55] Maya Patel: yes we can do a scoped billing export role. but two things — one: need to confirm which projects are included, two: we need to make sure KMS policies don't block the vendor from decrypting any payloads they legitimately need.
[01:12] Noah Kim: small nit, when you say KMS, do you mean the customer-managed keys we use for S3/Blob, or the internal envelope keys? sometimes folks mix the terms, could cause confusion.
[01:25] Lina Carter: good point. im referring to the envelope keys used for logs and vendor artifacts — the ones in the KMS vault. also one of the audit gaps was missing key-rotation notes.
[01:36] Olivia Reed: quick budget check: if we need to re-tag retroactively it will be manual and cost extra ops hours. FinOps can cover some but need sign-off from procurement.
[01:48] Ava Thompson: procurement here — we'll need a short memo for the vendor change and confirmation from FinOps that mapping is correct before we sign the SOW.
[01:58] Ethan Reyes: i'll own the mapping and will try to avoid retrofitting. plan is: create invoice->service tag spreadsheet and run a sample against last 30 days, flag untagged.
[02:12] Maya Patel: excellent. can you also add a column for project owner? that helps when security or platform need to escalate.
[02:20] Ethan Reyes: yup.
[02:22] Samir Banerjee: just to clarify, the vendor will not be able to edit billing data, only view exports.
[02:29] Noah Kim: for the delegation flow, we propose creating a dedicated service-account per vendor environment, pinned to a short-lived role via our token broker. that avoids long-lived keys.
[02:41] Lina Carter: yes, prefer token-broker approach. however, the token broker integration with our KMS is slightly different between cloud regions — we need to document region-specific steps.
[02:54] Maya Patel: ok can we make a decision now or do we need to escalate? I think token broker + per-vendor SA, plus RBAC filter for billing-export.
[03:05] Olivia Reed: sounds fine, but the finance team needs the tag schema first.
[03:11] Ethan Reyes: i'll produce the tag schema by Tue (2027-05-18) and start the reconcile.
[03:18] Lina Carter: i'll write the rotation steps and the exception path if there's an emergency access request. also add that any cross-region key access requires approval from security.
[03:30] Maya Patel: great. now one thing i want to highlight: we've been seeing intermittent failures in the vault API that cause service-account provisioning delays, which leads to vendors requesting manual creds. we must avoid manual creds.
[03:45] Noah Kim: yes the vault retry logic needs a small patch; i'll schedule the patch for Friday window unless we want hotfix. it's low risk.
[03:53] Samir Banerjee: from vendor mgmt: manual creds are a no-go for us for compliance reasons. we will accept short-lived tokens only.
[04:02] Maya Patel: understood.
[04:05] [04:05] (overlap) Ethan Reyes: quick question on billing exports — is there a way to give vendor access to only aggregated invoices rather than line items? that would reduce PII exposure.
[04:17] Lina Carter: yes we can provide an aggregated export. procurement if that meets your needs?
[04:22] Ava Thompson: aggregated is acceptable for now, but procurement wants the option to escalate to line items under NDA.
[04:30] Olivia Reed: financially aggregated might make it harder to map to service tags, but we can do a two-step process: aggregated for vendor, detailed for internal mapping only.
[04:42] Maya Patel: ok next topic, billing spike detection — we should set up a short-term alert for sudden egress or compute delta since new vendor runs in next week.
[04:54] Noah Kim: i'll add a billing anomaly alert: >20% delta day-over-day for vendor-tagged projects, email FinOps and page infra on-call.
[05:03] Ethan Reyes: page? better to email first then page if it persists > 2 hours. we dont want noisy pages overnight.
[05:12] Noah Kim: got it, email then page.
[05:14] Lina Carter: also add a security alert for unusual KMS decrypts from vendor service accounts.
[05:20] Maya Patel: good.
[05:23] [05:23] (crosstalk) Samir Banerjee: small ask — will you share the onboarding checklist so the vendor team can prep?
[05:29] Maya Patel: yes i'll share. liaison will be Noah and Samir.
[05:33] Samir Banerjee: thanks.
[05:35] Maya Patel: any blockers?
[05:37] Olivia Reed: only procurement sign-off; waiting on Ethan's mapping.
[05:42] Ethan Reyes: ok i'll prioritize it.
[05:45] Lina Carter: security: one more note, ensure RBAC comanaged roles are audited weekly during first month. that's an action item for security.
[05:55] Maya Patel: noted.
[05:57] [06:00] (brief pause)
[06:05] Maya Patel: let's go through owners and dates — Ethan, you said you'd have mapping by 2027-05-18
[06:11] Ethan Reyes: yes mapping by 5/18, reconcile sample by 5/20.
[06:16] Maya Patel: Lina key rotation runbook by 5/19
[06:19] Lina Carter: yep.
[06:21] Maya Patel: Noah patch for vault retry by 5/16 and monitor alert by 5/15
[06:27] Noah Kim: will do 5/16 for patch, alert in place 5/15.
[06:30] Maya Patel: procurement will hold SOW until Ethan shares mapping, procurement to confirm by 5/21
[06:36] Ava Thompson: correct.
[06:38] Maya Patel: ok last call-outs: don't create manual keys for vendors, use token broker; update the runbook link in the doc once Lina finishes.
[06:47] Samir Banerjee: got it, vendor side will stand by.
[06:50] Maya Patel: thanks all. i'll follow up with a thread and share the initial delegation table.
[06:55] Olivia Reed: thanks.
[06:57] [06:57] Meeting ended
